clue.text: Roughly punishes with pain ignoring one's misery

indicators.note: done roughly, the letters of the two words are knocked into a new, rough-and-ready order
ignoring says a letter from the combined pool is left out of the arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone describes how harsh, painful punishment leaves a person wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like it modifies 'punishes', but it signals the rearrangement; the pool has two Is and 'ignoring' drops one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name deep sadness or wretchedness, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: 'Bottom' fun, a director admits

indicators.note: the phrase admits, or holds within it, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: A film director concedes that a comedy, perhaps one called Bottom, was entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'fuN A DIRector'. The quotation marks on 'Bottom' make it look like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, such as a career or mood, is its rock bottom.

clue.text: A right shower reportedly in charge

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard spoken, giving a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A news item: a proper downpour has been reported in the area someone is responsible for.
explanation.walkthrough: The last part is pronounced like the wet-weather word but spelt -RAIGN; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse someone before a court is to bring them up on a charge.

clue.text: Pressure's on concerning cool house

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means about or concerning
fab, short for fabulous, means great or cool

explanation.surface: The pressure is on regarding a fashionable, cool home.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated building is a type of house, especially the post-war British temporary homes.

clue.text: Sick, showing common sense without a purpose

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first word wraps round the others

parts.note: nous is practical intelligence or common sense
a use is a purpose or function

explanation.surface: Someone feeling ill shows good judgement despite having no aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy, as though about to vomit, is being sick.

clue.text: Abuses cricketer oddly solo on boundaries

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in the odd-numbered places of the word

parts.note: edges are boundaries or borders

explanation.surface: A single cricket player is insulted while out on the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, sledging is taunting the batsman to break their concentration; 'on' is a link meaning placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket slang, fielders who taunt or verbally insult a batter are said to do this to him.

clue.text: Drops aitches it turned out, not right posh

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of the words are rearranged into a new form
not says one letter is to be excluded from the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Someone who drops their H sounds is, it emerges, not upper class after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping aitches (not pronouncing H) marks a non-posh accent, a British class marker. Rearrange DROPS AITCHES IT without its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh and refined both describe someone cultured and worldly, upper-class in manner.

clue.text: Stick criminal on very big island

parts.note: a bar is a rod or stick
bad means wicked or criminal
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very big

explanation.surface: A villain is hit with a stick on a large island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Caribbean island nation, so the clue names it by its category.

clue.text: Wandering about in art opening I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, a signal to rework the letters

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A personal musing about wandering through a gallery's new show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here; 'fancy' looks like a verb (I fancy) but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey from place to place, especially on foot, is a long wandering.

clue.text: Decree frontiers should have no boundaries

indicators.note: having no boundaries means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: borders are frontiers between countries

explanation.surface: A political statement that borders between nations ought to be abolished.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed letters are B and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An official command or edict issued by an authority is a decree.

clue.text: Count part return of asset a remuneration

indicators.note: return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
part says only a portion of the following words is taken, letters running across them

explanation.surface: An accountant counts part of what an asset earns, as with a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Count part' as the definition, but 'part' signals the hidden run (ETAREMUNE in 'assET A REMUNEration'); 'return of' then turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To list items one by one, numbering them, is to count them off.

clue.text: Legacy male's pinched leading to cell

indicators.note: pinched means squeezed, so one word grips the other inside it

parts.note: heritage is what is inherited, a legacy
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man's inheritance is stolen, which lands him in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' looks like stolen but means squeezed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse's dwelling, a single isolated room or retreat, is like a monk's cell.

clue.text: Place providing opening for birds in storm?

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind or storm

indicators.note: opening for takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question: where do birds find shelter or a way in during bad weather?
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' suggests a hole, but it means a first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular wall end under a pitched roof is a place on a building, often where birds nest.

clue.text: Back in a moment?

definitions.meaning: to back a motion is to support it formally
a brief instant, as in 'just a sec'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in a moment' reads as a shop-door sign; 'in a' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconding is supporting a proposal; a tiny unit of time also means an instant.

clue.text: Opera company hit featuring in church memorial

indicators.note: featuring in means placed within the following piece

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera
to tap is to hit lightly

explanation.surface: An opera troupe's popular show is staged in a church as a commemoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument honouring those buried elsewhere, especially war dead, is a memorial.

clue.text: Doctor is rude to stranger

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician is impolite to someone he doesn't know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, the subject, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not belonging to a group, an unfamiliar person, is a stranger.

clue.text: Smart and so vain, terribly offensive

parts.note: in means fashionable, as smart clothes are

indicators.note: terribly means badly, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of someone well dressed and so conceited that they are deeply unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' is a noun here, a military attack, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A military offensive into enemy territory is an incursion or attack of this kind.

clue.text: Clueless stupidly ranting about nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding the letter
stupidly means foolishly, signalling the letters are muddled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone without a clue ranting foolishly about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged RANTING (IGNRANT) goes about O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or awareness is to be without a clue, uninformed.

clue.text: Chauvinist admitting European's most saucy

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a racist is a bigot or chauvinist about race
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A bigot lets in a European who is the cheekiest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy means risque, so the superlative of racy fits the most suggestive.

clue.text: Section of 'Star' is endlessly followed

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part of a newspaper called the Star was endlessly read and followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' is part of the hiding place, not an instruction: the run is stAR IS ENdlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has arisen has resulted or come after, ensued, as consequences do.

clue.text: Class ruled and caused resentment

parts.note: rank is social class or standing
led means governed or ruled

explanation.surface: The ruling class's government bred bitterness among the people.
explanation.definitionFit: When a slight festers and causes bitterness, it is said to do this.

clue.text: Plan's south roughly around bottom edge?

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly
a hem is the bottom edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A plan for the south, roughly around its lower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan's' stands for 'plan is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or framework design is a plan in diagrammatic form.

clue.text: Room at the top in cottage initially

definitions.text: Room at the top in cottage initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: The uppermost room of a small country house.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'at the top in cottage' spell it, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A space just under the roof of a house is the loft, its topmost room.

clue.text: Rising in power while insincerity covers butt

parts.note: as means while, during the time that

indicators.note: covers means one word goes round the other

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, insincere talk
the butt is the end of something, as of a cigarette

explanation.surface: A rising politician's hypocrisy hides their weak point.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming dominant or more influential is to be on the rise, in the ascendant.

clue.text: Lots of winners accepting silver finally

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: aces are winning serves in tennis, or high cards

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Many champions are taking silver medals at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Lots here are plots of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Land is measured in these units, so plots of land are counted by them; also informally lots, plenty.

clue.text: Former favourite compiler's receiving large curse

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: receiving means taking another piece inside

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
the compiler says I've, short for I have

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, once popular, has received a lot of swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler's' is the setter speaking: I'VE, here 'compiler has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word or oath is a curse.

clue.text: Slow early bird doesn't finish work

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lark is a person who rises early, an early bird
to go is to function or work

explanation.surface: A sluggish early riser fails to complete their task.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a musical tempo marking, from Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: As a musical direction, it instructs players to perform slowly and broadly.

clue.text: 'Get up, get up!', to welcome duke's regiment

parts.note: to stand is to get up

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to arise is to get up
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: An order to rise and greet a nobleman's military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regiment' is a verb here, not the army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment is to impose strict uniformity, to make everything conform.
